incidents.vector: Intruders accessed the benefits-administration platform's network and exfiltrated files over a five-day window in November before the company was later listed on the Akira ransomware leak site.
incidents.impact: Stolen data on tens of thousands of people included Social Security numbers, financial account details, health insurance and medical data, passport numbers and taxpayer IDs; over 64,000 South Carolina residents plus victims in multiple other states were affected, spurring class-action suits.

incidents.vector: A large-scale distributed denial-of-service attack flooded the infrastructure of Digdir's IT partner Vivicta, two to three times larger than prior incidents.
incidents.impact: Ten digital services were disrupted for more than a day, including the ID-porten identity gateway used by 4.5 million people, degrading logins to government services, online pharmacies and Norway's e-prescription system; it was the third DDoS to hit Digdir since June.

incidents.vector: An actor using the persona 'CyberLeek' obtained a pre-release build of Grand Theft Auto VI — likely via an insider or direct access to Rockstar systems — and drip-published gameplay footage a week before the planned reveal.
incidents.impact: Daily leaks of unreleased footage triggered a major legal response (DMCA subpoenas against Discord, Microsoft, X and Google) as CyberLeek monetized via a memecoin and watermarked crypto wallet links; the leaks threaten the launch of a title projected to earn billions.

incidents.vector: West African organized-crime networks including Black Axe ran romance scams, investment/cryptocurrency scams and business email compromise, supported by crime-as-a-service domain and money-laundering providers.
incidents.impact: An Interpol operation across 22 countries produced 58 arrests and 263 identified suspects; police seized millions in assets, including a Romanian call-center scam valued at ~$166 million and a South African syndicate targeting elderly victims.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (energy, water, defense, healthcare, IT, financial)
incidents.vector: A MOIS-directed team breached corporate email accounts and networks across critical-infrastructure sectors since late 2023, including attacks on water-system operational technology in at least 12 states.
incidents.impact: The US Treasury sanctioned six Iranian nationals (four also indicted) for compromising energy companies, defense contractors, healthcare, IT and financial institutions, plus local, state and federal offices; some members also pursued personal financial gain and cryptocurrency theft.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused the legitimate TWCore update application on Chinese-made DoFun in-car head units to silently push malicious 'JarService' code without any driver interaction.
incidents.impact: Infected head units were turned into reverse proxies and ad-fraud nodes as part of a botnet, letting other people's traffic route through the car's connection; Kaspersky attributed the campaign to the MoYu Group linked to the BadBox operation.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-73570, an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Zimbra's SNMP notification handling (enabled by default) reachable via crafted SMTP requests.
incidents.impact: CISA added the bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered federal agencies to patch within three days after active exploitation and a CERT Polska warning; compromised mail servers expose messages, calendars and contacts useful for follow-on attacks.

incidents.vector: Attackers registered their own Microsoft 365 tenant to pose as an IT service desk, hosted a fake PowerShell tool on Microsoft Azure storage, and deployed the modular Python-based 'SynkLoader' malware.
incidents.impact: The multi-tool loader profiles victim networks (a hallmark of ransomware pre-staging), maintains persistence via COM, provides remote access and screen takeover, and includes a 'PhishLocker' fake Windows lock screen to harvest SSO passwords; researchers assess it as a precursor to follow-on ransomware.

incidents.vector: Iranian actors intruded on a small British power plant reportedly involving a programmable logic controller (PLC) that was not secured.
incidents.impact: The facility was shut down for four days, though no customers lost power and the wider grid was unaffected; officials called it a major escalation from earlier water-utility targeting and briefed energy-sector CEOs on defensive steps.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed the Latvian road-traffic agency and exfiltrated citizen records; the intrusion method was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The personal details of 1.2 million Latvians — including payment receipts and license-plate data going back to 2008 — were stolen; officials warned of scams and the CSDD leadership resigned.

incidents.vector: A threat actor listed government data for sale on an underground forum; officials denied a breach of eGov systems and said the data was likely taken from another agency connected to the government database.
incidents.impact: The exposed data covers roughly 15 million citizens — about three-quarters of Kazakhstan's population — and is being offered for sale.

incidents.victim: Internet-exposed Windows and Linux web servers (UAT-10147)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking crime group exploited publicly disclosed one-day vulnerabilities (Zimbra, AjaxPro, Nacos and Linux privilege-escalation bugs) at scale, using AI-generated playbooks and automation plus custom implants like SPECTRE and BadIIS.
incidents.impact: The actor achieved remote code execution across servers in Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam for SEO fraud and data theft, deploying rootkits, BYOVD EDR-killer capabilities and persistence from a target list of ~170,000 URLs.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a popular Rust developer's account and injected malware into three of his libraries in a supply-chain attack; Wiz linked the attacker infrastructure to known North Korean operations.
incidents.impact: The malicious versions were live for only 23 minutes but one affected package, Arrayref, has nearly 5 million weekly downloads; the Rust security team removed the versions and locked the developer's account.

incidents.vector: Slovakia's NBU found that NERO R-ONE speed cameras — a rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M model — contained a backdoor granting shell and network access via SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers, alongside disabled SecureBoot and open unauthenticated live streams.
incidents.impact: The Interior Ministry paused deployment of 279 cameras bought under a €30 million EU-funded project and ordered an independent audit; similar devices are reportedly installed in Croatia and other Eastern European countries.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack struck the Berlin city government's transport and urban development departments; details of the initial access vector were not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Emails, remote gateways and internet connections were knocked out across the two departments, and IT staff disconnected them from the city network to prevent the incident from spreading.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack hit systems at Winnipeg's largest hospital, disabling building-control and access systems.
incidents.impact: Access doors and heating, ventilation and air conditioning were disabled, forcing the hospital to increase on-site security while the access-card system remained down; the hospital said patient care and clinical operations were not impacted.

incidents.victim: Universities, companies and government agencies (Mabna Institute)
incidents.vector: The Iran-based Mabna Institute ran spearphishing campaigns against professor accounts and corporate/government email systems on behalf of the IRGC and other Iranian clients from 2013 through at least 2017.
incidents.impact: A superseding indictment charged 17 Iranians for stealing at least 31.5 terabytes of academic data and IP from 144 US and 178 foreign universities plus dozens of companies and government agencies; the US offered up to $10 million in rewards for five defendants.

incidents.vector: An Iranian hacktivist group calling itself the '313 Team' launched distributed denial-of-service attacks against the two platforms on consecutive days.
incidents.impact: The attacks caused prolonged outages at BlueSky and GitHub; the same group ran an earlier DDoS wave in April and BlueSky said it upgraded its defenses in response.

incidents.victim: French Directorate General of Public Finance (DGFiP)
incidents.vector: A hacker using the handle 'ZeroBytes' breached the French tax agency between June and July and began exfiltrating taxpayer data before detection.
incidents.impact: The tax information of more than 678,000 French citizens was stolen; the actor claimed to have been downloading data on up to 20 million people before access was cut off.

incidents.vector: Hackers stole customer data from Israel's largest cryptocurrency exchange via an external analytics service provider.
incidents.impact: The data of 250,000 customers was compromised; the company notified customers over the weekend but did not specify what type of data was taken.

incidents.victim: Payment and shopping platform users (JWR phishing)
incidents.vector: An undocumented phishing framework branded 'JWR' — assessed as a variant of the Chinese-speaking 'Outsider' PhaaS platform — impersonated checkout and login flows for Shopify, PayPal, Apple, Klarna and banks, using an encrypted WebSocket to let operators steer victim sessions live.
incidents.impact: The kit harvested full payment card data, credentials, SSNs, passport/ID images, 2FA codes and device fingerprints in real time; a live campaign delivered it via SMS lures impersonating toll authorities and postal/courier services across Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to the French shipping and logistics firm's systems and began leaking stolen customer data on the dark web.
incidents.impact: Freight delivery was disrupted across large parts of Europe, affecting customers including Valve's Steam hardware business and Dutch retailers Bol and De Bijenkorf, with days- to weeks-long delivery delays.

incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese hackers used publicly available AI tools — a framework of Hermes and OpenClaw agents — to automate reconnaissance, initial access, lateral movement and data exfiltration against government networks.
incidents.impact: The campaign breached Taiwanese government networks and Thailand's Ministry of Finance as part of a wider wave hitting multiple Asian governments, per Dream Security.
